title: Damian and the Halloween Lights
summary: On Halloween night, Damian, in the superhero cape and cardboard rocket-pack he engineered himself, leads his costumed friends along a dark wire to find why the pumpkin lights went out, gently frees a tangled kitten and lights up Lantern Lane again.
character: Damian, a cheerful young boy with short tousled brown hair, big brown eyes and rosy cheeks, wearing a bright red superhero cape, a navy blue long-sleeved shirt and navy pants, red sneakers, and a homemade rocket-pack on his back made of two silver-painted cardboard boxes with two paper-towel-tube boosters and orange tissue-paper flames

pages.text: On Halloween night, Damian zoomed down the hall in the costume he had built all by himself. He had a swishy red cape and a shiny rocket-pack made from cardboard boxes, paper-towel tubes and orange tissue-paper flames. "Captain Rocket, ready for blast-off!" he announced.

pages.text: Damian had engineered every part. The straps were snug, the flames fluttered, and a big button on the front went click! "Tonight," he said, "Captain Rocket will help anyone who needs a hand." Then he grabbed his pumpkin bucket and marched out into the cool, crunchy night.

pages.text: On the corner, his friends were waiting. Maya was a firefighter with a shiny red helmet. Leo was a pirate with a striped shirt and a spyglass. Priya was a wizard in a starry purple hat, and Sam was an astronaut in a puffy white suit. "Happy Halloween!" they all shouted.

pages.text: Lantern Lane was the most wonderful street in town. A long string of glowing pumpkin lights looped from porch to porch, all the way to the pumpkin patch party at the end. The friends skipped from door to door. "Trick or treat!" "Thank you!" Their buckets grew heavier and heavier.

pages.text: Then, all at once, blink, blink, fizzle! Every pumpkin light on Lantern Lane went dark. The porch lights still glowed softly and the stars still twinkled, but the long, cheerful string of pumpkins was gone. "Oh no," said a little girl dressed as a ladybug. "How will we find the pumpkin patch party?"

pages.text: "Don't worry," said Damian, tapping his chin like a real engineer. "Lights need electricity, and electricity travels along the wire. If we follow the wire, we can find the problem!" Maya clicked on her flashlight. Sam switched on his helmet lamp. "Team Halloween," said Damian, "let's investigate!"
pages.scene: Damian taps his chin thoughtfully, pointing at a long green electrical cord running along the bottom of a fence; Maya shines her flashlight on the cord and Sam's helmet lamp glows; Leo and Priya lean in eagerly. pages.text: Step by step, the friends followed the long green wire past pumpkins and porches. Leo peered through his spyglass. "The wire goes behind that hay bale!" he whispered. Then they heard a teeny, tiny sound. "Mew. Mew." Something behind the hay bale was wiggling.

pages.text: Priya lifted her flashlight. There sat a fluffy little gray kitten, all tangled up in the wire like a ball of yarn. She had been playing, and she had pulled the plug right out! "Poor little kitty," said Damian softly. "Don't worry. We'll help you."

pages.text: Damian knelt down slowly so the kitten would not be frightened. "Gentle hands," he reminded his friends. Maya held the flashlight steady while Priya stroked the kitten's soft head. Damian carefully unwound one loop, then another, then another. "There you go," he whispered. The kitten purred.

pages.text: Now for the plug. Captain Rocket knew that plugs are a job for grown-ups, so he called, "Excuse me! Can you help us, please?" Mrs. Alvarez from the yellow house came hurrying over. She smiled, picked up the plug and pushed it back into the outdoor socket. Click!

pages.text: Blink, blink, GLOW! All along Lantern Lane, the pumpkin lights flickered back on, one after another, like a parade of little orange moons. Everyone cheered, "Hooray for Team Halloween!" Snuggled safe in Damian's arms, the kitten gave a happy little "Mew!"

pages.text: At the pumpkin patch party, a little boy in a dinosaur costume came running. "My kitten! You found her!" Damian gently handed her over. Then the friends sipped warm apple cider and shared their treats. "Clever thinking and kind hearts," said Mrs. Alvarez. Damian's cheeks glowed as orange as the pumpkins.

pages.text: Later, Damian walked home beneath the glowing lights, his bucket full and his cape swishing slowly. He hung up his rocket-pack, brushed his teeth and snuggled under his cozy blanket. Outside, the pumpkin lights twinkled. "Goodnight, Lantern Lane," Damian whispered, and he drifted off to sleep.
